context: The redesign (:59-67) makes test adequacy three layers: structural (a bound test enters only through the app entry, stand-ins only at the network edge and the clock, assertions on captured logs and outbound calls, factories never silently default a logger, emitter or sender), the mutation proof (break each Code Node symbol of a touched criterion: stub to throw, no-op, remove the call; at least one bound test must go red), and Review's judgement. The operator kept mutation in v1 with exactly those three operators and no general mutation testing (09:20Z answer 2). Q-07 a needs the app entry defined for a CLI or library. Cause 3 of the redesign: tests built the app's parts themselves.
decision: A project declares its entry, harness, edge and clock in rcf/test-strength.json (test-author, criteria class); no declaration exits 2 rather than guessing. For a CLI the entry is its bin spawned as a child process (rcf-lite: bin/rcf.js, through the shared harness, or the packed artefact); for a library, its package exports imported by package name; for a Worker-style app, the module its deploy configuration names as main, built as production builds it and called through the harness. The structural check is static: every import in a bound test file resolves to a Node builtin, a third-party dependency, the harness or the entry (any other product file is a finding); a module mock is allowed only on a declared edge or clock specifier; a Code Node symbol whose parameter or destructured option named logger, log, emitter, events, sender, mailer or notifier has a default value is a silent-default finding. Whether a test asserts on the captured logs and outbound calls the criterion names is Review's judgement, not the tool's. Mutants are applied in a scratch git worktree under the OS temp directory at HEAD, one at a time per job, and only the touched criterion's bound tests run against each; a mutant that times out counts as killed and is listed as timeout; call removal with no statement-level call site is notApplicable. A file-level Code Node on a source file (.js, .mjs, .cjs) is never mutated, because source code needs symbol granularity: a criterion with one and no symbol-level Code Node fails with "no symbol-level Code Node". A file-level Code Node on a code file in another language (.ts .tsx .jsx .py .rb .go .java .kt .rs .php .cs .swift) exits 2 as not a supported source, as do a bound test file and a symbol-level Code Node outside .js, .mjs and .cjs. A file-level Code Node on any other path (docs, JSON, YAML, .github/ workflows, chain records) gets a fourth operator, fileBlank: the file is blanked in the scratch worktree, the criterion's bound tests run, and at least one must go red (decision 103, the operator's answer (c); the order of these path rules is decision 104). The verifier records the result at TEST with --record, beside the TEST verdict, and Finalise reads it.
consequences: Test strength costs symbols times three operators, plus one fileBlank mutant per file-level Code Node on a non-source path, times the bound tests' run time, and slice scope keeps it cheap: a round touching 8 criteria of a 152-criterion spec mutates only those 8 criteria's symbols. rcf-lite's own pre-0.37.0 tests that import src/ internals would fail the structural check, which bites only on criteria a later round touches; the 0.37.0 tests part B writes go through bin/rcf.js. Code Nodes earn their keep: a criterion with none cannot pass.

alternativesConsidered.name: Infer the entry from package.json
alternativesConsidered.summary: Take bin or main as the entry without a declaration.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A Worker's entry is in its deploy configuration and a monorepo has several packages; a wrong guess would pass or fail tests silently.

alternativesConsidered.name: General mutation testing
alternativesConsidered.summary: Operator sets such as Stryker's over all code.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Ruled out by the operator (09:20Z answer 2); cost scales with the codebase rather than the round.

alternativesConsidered.name: Run the tool in CI on every push
alternativesConsidered.summary: CI runs test strength instead of the verifier.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Its cost belongs to the touched criteria of one round; recording it at TEST beside the suite run ties it to the reviewed head Finalise judges.

title: Test strength v1: a declared entry and harness, three mutation operators on symbol-level Code Nodes and fileBlank on file-level Code Nodes of non-source paths, mutants in a scratch worktree, recorded at TEST
